source_evidence.anchor: [E1] Exercise 2.5.10 opening sentence: ‘Let X₁, X₂, ... be a sequence of sub-gaussian random variables, which are not necessarily independent.’
source_evidence.observation: The objects form a countably indexed sequence of sub-gaussian random variables, and the source expressly says that independence is not required.

source_evidence.anchor: [E2] Exercise 2.5.10 first displayed claim immediately after ‘Show that’
source_evidence.observation: The displayed target is 𝔼 max_i (|X_i| / √(1 + log i)) ≤ C K. The maximum is written over an unbounded index i; no finite cutoff appears in this first display.

source_evidence.anchor: [E3] The where-clause immediately following the first display: ‘where K = max_i ‖X_i‖_{ψ₂}.’
source_evidence.observation: K is defined using the source's literal maximum of the ψ₂ norms across the same sequence.

The hint says to set Y_i := X_i/(C K √(1 + log i)) with an absolute constant C chosen sufficiently large, use the sub-gaussian tail bound (2.14) and a union bound to obtain ℙ{∃ i : |Y_i| ≥ t} ≲ exp(−t²) for t ≥ 1, and then use the integrated-tail formula (Lemma 1.2.1), splitting the integral over [0,1] and [1,∞).

A random variable satisfying any one of properties (i)–(iv) of Proposition 2.5.2 is called sub-gaussian. Its sub-gaussian norm is the smallest K₄ in property (iv), stated exactly as ‖X‖_{ψ₂} = inf { t > 0 : 𝔼 exp(X²/t²) ≤ 2 }.

source_evidence.anchor: [E6] Restatement of Proposition 2.5.2, displayed tail bound (2.14), and the sentence ‘Here C, c > 0 are absolute constants.’
source_evidence.observation: The tail bound referenced by the hint is ℙ{|X| ≥ t} ≤ 2 exp(−c t²/‖X‖²_{ψ₂}) for every t ≥ 0, with c > 0 absolute.

source_evidence.anchor: [E7] Sentence beginning ‘Deduce that for every N ≥ 2’ and its subsequent second display
source_evidence.observation: The finite-N estimate is a separate deduction after the first displayed claim and is outside this task's selected claim.

binders: [E1] X₁, X₂, ... is a sequence indexed by i = 1, 2, ... of random variables.
[E2,E4] C > 0 is one absolute constant, chosen universally and sufficiently large rather than depending on i or on the particular sequence.
[E3] K is the quantity K := max_i ‖X_i‖_{ψ₂}.
hypotheses: [E1,E5] Every X_i is sub-gaussian in the sense of Definition 2.5.6.
[E1] The variables are not required to be independent.
[E1,E5] No centering or mean-zero hypothesis is stated; Definition 2.5.6 invokes properties (i)–(iv), whose use here does not add a centering condition.
conclusions: [E2,E3] 𝔼[max_i |X_i|/√(1 + log i)] ≤ C K, where the same unbounded index i runs through the sequence and K = max_i ‖X_i‖_{ψ₂}.
definitions_and_conventions: [E5] Exact ψ₂ definition: ‖X‖_{ψ₂} = inf { t > 0 : 𝔼 exp(X²/t²) ≤ 2 }.
[E5] ‘Sub-gaussian’ means that X satisfies one of the equivalent properties (i)–(iv) in Proposition 2.5.2; the ψ₂ norm is the smallest K₄ from property (iv).
[E3] The exercise defines K by the literal notation max_i ‖X_i‖_{ψ₂}, not by a finite-N maximum.
[E4,E6] The hint's referenced tail convention is ℙ{|X| ≥ t} ≤ 2 exp(−c t²/‖X‖²_{ψ₂}) for all t ≥ 0, with an absolute c > 0.
implicit_context: [E1,E2] The indices are the positive integers, as indicated by X₁, X₂, ... and log i.
[E1,E2] Because a maximum and probability event involving all X_i are formed, the variables must be jointly realized on a common probability space; the source does not state this separately.
[E2,E4] The expectation is of the logarithmically weighted countable maximum max_i(|X_i|/√(1 + log i)).
[E7] Only the first display is in scope; the later finite-N deduction is not part of this contract.

details: [E1,E2,E4] The claim applies to an arbitrary countable sequence of sub-gaussian variables and uses one absolute C; C is not an index-dependent or distribution-dependent family of constants.
[E1] Dependence among the X_i is allowed explicitly.
[E1,E5] No hypothesis 𝔼X_i = 0 occurs in the exercise or in the operative ψ₂ definition.
[E2] The quantity inside expectation is max_i |X_i|/√(1 + log i), with the weight attached separately to each positive-integer index and no truncation N.
[E4] Normalize each variable as Y_i := X_i/(C K √(1 + log i)) using a sufficiently large absolute C.
[E4,E6] Apply (2.14) to each Y_i and then a union bound to reach ℙ{∃ i : |Y_i| ≥ t} ≲ exp(−t²) for every t ≥ 1.
[E4] Integrate the tail via Lemma 1.2.1, splitting at t = 1 into [0,1] and [1,∞).
[E2,E7] The contract contains the first displayed countable-sequence estimate only and excludes the subsequent finite-N corollary.

undebatable_constraints: [E1,E2] Preserve the countably infinite sequence X₁, X₂, ... and the unbounded index in the first displayed maximum.
[E1] Do not add independence; the source expressly says it is unnecessary.
[E1,E5] Do not add centering or mean-zero assumptions.
[E3] Preserve K = max_i ‖X_i‖_{ψ₂} exactly as written.
[E2] Preserve the expected logarithmically weighted maximum 𝔼[max_i |X_i|/√(1 + log i)].
[E2,E4] Use one positive absolute constant C, universal for the claim.
[E5] Preserve the exact norm definition ‖X‖_{ψ₂} = inf { t > 0 : 𝔼 exp(X²/t²) ≤ 2 }.
[E4] Preserve the hint's normalization, appeal to (2.14), countable union bound, exp(−t²)-type tail for t ≥ 1, and integrated-tail split at 1.
[E7] Do not include the subsequent finite-N deduction in this selected first-claim contract.

ambiguities.issue: The source writes max_i for a countably infinite sequence, without saying whether this denotes an attained maximum or a supremum.
ambiguities.evidence: [E1,E2] The sequence is X₁, X₂, ... and the first display literally uses max_i with no cutoff.
ambiguities.impact: A formal statement must either preserve an appropriate countable maximum/supremum meaning or explicitly justify an attained maximum; it must not silently replace the sequence by a finite family.

ambiguities.issue: The source likewise writes K = max_i ‖X_i‖_{ψ₂} without stating that this maximum is attained or finite.
ambiguities.evidence: [E3] The where-clause contains literal max_i notation and gives no uniform-boundedness or attainment hypothesis.
ambiguities.impact: Encoding K as a finite real maximum would add an unstated assumption; encoding it as a supremum or extended-real quantity requires an explicit interpretive choice. The hint's division by K also presumes a usable finite positive normalization.

ambiguities.issue: The logarithm base is not specified in the exercise.
ambiguities.evidence: [E2,E4] Both the display and the hint use ‘log i’ without a local definition of log.
ambiguities.impact: The literal notation should be preserved or the conventional logarithm choice documented; changing bases modifies the weight by constants that may be absorbed into an absolute C but is not textually specified.

ambiguities.issue: A common probability space for the entire sequence is semantically needed but not stated explicitly.
ambiguities.evidence: [E1,E2,E4] The source calls the X_i a sequence and forms both max_i |X_i| and the event ∃i : |Y_i| ≥ t.
ambiguities.impact: A formalization needs a shared probability space to express the countable maximum and union event; adding it is an explicit realization of implicit context, not an extra probabilistic independence assumption.

ambiguities.issue: The hint divides by K without separately treating the degenerate case K = 0.
ambiguities.evidence: [E3,E4] K is defined as the maximum ψ₂ norm and Y_i is then defined by division by C K; no K > 0 condition or zero case is stated.
ambiguities.impact: A proof formalization may need to split off K = 0, but the theorem contract must not strengthen the hypotheses by silently assuming K > 0.

contract_plain_english: [E1–E3,E5] For any countable sequence X₁, X₂, ... of sub-gaussian random variables—without independence and without centering—let K be the source's max_i ‖X_i‖_{ψ₂}, where exactly ‖X‖_{ψ₂} = inf {t > 0 : 𝔼 exp(X²/t²) ≤ 2}. One absolute constant C bounds the expectation of the countable logarithmically weighted maximum: 𝔼[max_i |X_i|/√(1 + log i)] ≤ C K. [E4] The hint normalizes by C K √(1 + log i), uses the ψ₂ tail bound and a union bound to get an exp(−t²)-type tail for t ≥ 1, and integrates that tail after splitting at 1. [E7] The later finite-N deduction is deliberately excluded.
